name: NPC Reaction Rules
description: Reusable tag-driven NPC reaction guidelines. These rules are not automatic dialogue yet; they define consistent authoring hooks for passive reactions, greetings, suspicion, respect, kinship, and faction prejudice.

reaction_axes.name: Martial Respect
reaction_axes.summary: Soldiers, guards, mercenaries, caravan hands, and hard-bitten villagers recognize credible combat or guard experience.
reaction_axes.tone: measured respect, less posturing, more practical detail
sample_lines: You stand like someone who has watched a road turn bad before.
I will not waste your time with tavern stories. Here is what matters.

reaction_axes.name: Arcane Suspicion
reaction_axes.summary: Priests, guards, commoners, and frightened villagers distrust visible magic, occult sensitivity, or unnatural marks.
reaction_axes.tone: guarded, fearful, testing boundaries, invoking iron or faith
sample_lines: Keep your hands where I can see them, mage.
Old stones wake for people like you. That is rarely a kindness.

reaction_axes.name: Commoner Kinship
reaction_axes.summary: Laborers, outcasts, drifters, and hungry villagers open up to characters with believable hardship or common roots.
reaction_axes.tone: plainspoken, less formal, more personal detail
sample_lines: You know what a bad winter does to honest folk. So listen close.
A noble would not notice this, but you might.

reaction_axes.name: Noble Recognition and Prejudice
reaction_axes.summary: Nobles, officials, officers, rebels, and debt-holders react strongly to noble blood, exile, and political reputation.
reaction_axes.tone: formal recognition, veiled contempt, old debts, political caution
sample_lines: That name still buys silence in some rooms and knives in others.
I wondered whether you would speak like a courtier or an exile.

reaction_axes.name: Underworld Distrust
reaction_axes.summary: Guards and honest merchants distrust underworld ties, while thieves and informants may speak more openly.
sample_lines: People who sell secrets rarely stop at one buyer.
If you know the quiet price, do not make me say it aloud.

reaction_axes.name: Healer Utility
reaction_axes.summary: The sick, wounded, desperate, and practical authorities value medicine and field surgery even when they dislike the character personally.
sample_lines: If you know wounds, stop talking and look at this one.
I do not care what you charge. Tell me if she will live.

authoring_rules: Use reactions as seasoning, not replacement characterization.
Prefer one short recognition line before returning to the scene's actual problem.
NPCs should react according to their own fears, class position, faction, and immediate need.
A tag can unlock trust, suspicion, price changes, alternate clues, or unique insults.
Do not make every NPC comment on every visible tag; repetition makes tags feel mechanical.
When two tags conflict, prefer the NPC's strongest bias or the local situation. A starving villager may tolerate a mage if the mage can heal a child.
